verdict.reasoning: Linear fits on company size (201-500 headcount, roughly 270-290 per Tracxn), funding stage (Series C, $82M in June 2025) and budget ($100M ARR, cashflow positive, $134M raised) per web search sources [16][18]. Slack is confirmed in the tech stack [2][8] and a finance tool (Mercury) is listed, but no finance-leader hiring roles appear and Linear sells project management software, not spend management, so it is not a competitor. Confidence is medium because headcount figures conflict and the tools listing shows no NetSuite, QuickBooks, Expensify or Workday.

signals.text: Company size: 201-500 headcount range, with the latest data point at 291 employees (Aug 2026), inside the 50-1000 target.
Funding stage and budget: Series C ($82M, June 2025, led by Accel), $134M total raised and about $100M ARR, so mid-market budget capacity is clear.

Technology: Slack is in the stack; Mercury is used for finance. No ERP or expense tool (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Expensify, Workday) was found, and no finance roles are open (hiring is engineering, design, GTM, recruiting).

verdict.next_step: Contact the Head of Finance or Operations (no Controller or VP of Finance posting is visible, so confirm who owns finance). Open with the growth story ($100M ARR, remote-first team across many locations, plus the August 2026 secondary) and ask how they handle card spend and expense workflows beyond Mercury.

**Fundamentals**
**Linear (linear.app)**

- **Funding stage:** Series C. The latest priced round was a Series C on Jun 10, 2025, for $82M. A later secondary sale reportedly valued the company at about $2.5B. The sale was structured so that $99M went to employees rather than to Linear's balance sheet. That means it wasn't new primary funding.
- **Total funding:** about $134M. Sacra puts the figure at $134.2M across all rounds. Tracxn and Multiples agree on roughly $134M.
- **Employee headcount:** sources disagree.
  - PitchBook lists 141 employees as of 2026, but its page looks older.
  - Tracxn reports 291 as of Aug 31, 2026.
  - Another tracker shows 269 employees as of 2026-07-01.
  - The most recent data points to roughly 270–290.
- **Founding year:** 2019. The founders are Karri Saarinen, Jori Lallo, and Tuomas Artman.
- **Headquarters:** San Francisco, California.
- **Revenue estimate:** about $100M in annual recurring revenue. Sacra estimates Linear hit $100M ARR in July 2026. One older ZoomInfo-based estimate of $42M also appears, but it is likely outdated.

**Recent news**
# Linear: key news, 2025–2026

## Funding and valuation
- **Series C, June 2025.** Linear raised $82M at a $1.25B valuation. The round included primary and secondary funding and was led by Accel, with continued support from Sequoia and 01A. New backers included Seven Seven Six and Designer Fund.
- **Use of funds.** The money was meant to speed up product development, including deeper AI and agent capabilities.
- **Secondary sale, August 2026.** One aggregator reports a secondary sale at a $2.5B valuation, led by Accel with Salesforce Ventures, S32 and 01 Advisors participating. The amount is listed as $99M in one place and $100M in another. The same source says the money went to employees, not the company's balance sheet. I only found this on aggregator sites, so treat it as less certain.
- **Profitability.** Linear has been cashflow positive since 2021 and holds more cash than it has ever raised in primary funding.

## Growth
- **Revenue.** A February 2026 profile reported more than 20,000 customer companies and $100M in 2025 revenue. Linear's own site now claims more than 40,000 product teams.
- **Customers.** Named customers include OpenAI, Cursor, Ramp, Coinbase, Cash App and Oscar Health.
- **Hiring.** Headcount figures conflict across sources: 118 employees, roughly 160 to 190, and 269. The company grows slowly and stays remote. I found no reliable report of specific hires or executive changes.

## Product launches
- **Linear Diffs, 2026.** A way to review PRs directly inside Linear, listed on Product Hunt as launched May 29, 2026. Stacked PR support has since been added.
- **Linear Agent, March 24, 2026.** Public beta, free on all plans during the beta. Agents are full workspace members that can be assigned issues and mentioned in comments. It was followed by Code Intelligence and MCP support.
- **Shared Skills, June 4, 2026.** Lets teams save and reuse agent instructions.
- **Coding Sessions, June 11, 2026.** Linear Agent can now write code using Claude Code and Codex. It is generally available on Basic, Business and Enterprise plans, and AI credits are required.
- **Loops, July 20, 2026.** Recurring agent automations that run on a schedule or in response to an event. They are available on Business and Enterprise plans.
- **Smaller releases.** These include a Priority inbox (Sept 3), Loops scheduling options (Sept 4) and agent-drafted projects (Sept 8). Other recent additions are agent-assisted project updates and private sub-teams.

## Partnerships and integrations
- **Coding agents.** The coding-agent features build on Claude Code and Codex. The changelog also lists GPT-5.6 Luna as a model option and GitHub Copilot for Linear.
- **Integrations.** In June 2026 Linear announced integrations with Slack, Notion, Discord, Glean, Attio, Figma, Descript, YouTube, Miro, Loom and Tella. It also added compliance tools such as Vanta, Drata and Orca Security.
- **Sequoia.** Linear appeared in a May 2026 Startup Grind conversation with Sequoia Capital about AI agents.

## Setbacks and caveats
- **Security incident.** Linear published a post-mortem on a security incident on March 24, 2026. I did not open it, so I can't give details.
- **User complaints.** Some users report slow first-page loads, sync bugs, and growing complexity.
- **Acquisition claim.** One aggregator says Linear "was acquired." Other sources describe it as an independently run, venture-backed private company, so I'd disregard that claim.

I can look further into the March 2026 security incident or the details of the August secondary sale if you'd like.
